description: Day 1: Taking a boat ride to Goodwin Islands to set lift nets. Involves digging small trench and setting PVC poles. Also count marsh shoot density with quadrat. Day 2: Collect from lift nets and suction sample (like a big underwater vacuum) adjacent habitats for juvenile blue crabs and measure them. Take seagrass cores.
qualification: Must have your own transport to VIMS. Must be comfortable working long hours outside. Must be comfortable traveling by boat and swimming. We will at most be in 3.5ft depth of water, but swimming is important for safety.

opportunity_name: Fish infectious disease ecology and evolution research
description: The Wargo lab at VIMS is seeking undergraduates to assist with research in the ecology and evolution of infectious diseases in fish. This could include assisting with fish care, processing samples using molecular tools such as quantitative PCR, setup and takedown of experiments, vaccination of fish, studies of microplastic impacts on fish, virus detection and quantification, bacteriology, and general laboratory maintenance. Students will be trained in a variety of basic laboratory skills, which may lead to opportunities for independent research. Volunteer positions typically transition into paid, for credit, or summer hires. Please send a CV and statement of interest to arwargo@vims.edu.
qualification: Any of the following are desired but not required: Microbiology Molecular biology Virology Bacteriology Animal care
compensation_details: Positions typically start as volunteer but can transition into academic credit or paid

description: The Communities & Coasts Lab is looking for undergraduates to work on a research project reconstructing historic marine food webs in Alaska. Undergraduate researchers will assist in identifying archaeological bird bones.
The Coastal Ecogeomorphology Lab is looking for volunteers to assist with soil processing. Main tasks include processing wetland soil samples for salinity and organic matter.

Oyster microbiome will be analyzed using 16S metabarcoding techniques. Student will be trained to conduct DNA extraction, PCR of 16S genes and Miseq sequencing. Bioinformatic analysis of sequence data can be included depending on the student's interests.

I have a large historical dataset of microbial communities associated with multiple intertidal seaweed species taken from across the North Atlantic. The student will help with data analysis and preparation of final manuscript. Previous publication with the dataset can be viewed here: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/jpy.13194
A postdoc in the Coastal and Estuarine Ecology Lab is seeking undergraduates to assist with processing seagrass, clam, and sediment samples.

opportunity_name: Environmental Microbiology with a focus on Vibrio bacteria
description: We are seeking an undergraduate student who would be interested in environmental microbiology. Our research focuses on Vibrio bacteria, in particular species pathogenic to oysters or humans, with an interest in better understanding the ecology of these bacteria in their host and in the environment. The student would assist in general lab maintenance and would be involved in processing samples using microbiological techniques and molecular methods such as standard PCR and quantitative PCR. The student will work closely with the principal investigator and a technician. If interested, please contact Dr. Corinne Audemard (audemard@vims.edu).
academic_term: Start Fall 2026 with possibility to continue into 2027
compensation_details: Start as a volunteer position with opportunities to get an hourly position
